content: PLUNC, also known as Palate, Lung, and Nasal Epithelium Clone Protein, is a gene that encodes a secretory protein. This protein is alternatively referred to as Secretory Protein in Upper Respiratory Tracts (SPURT). In humans, it is encoded by the BPIFA1 gene, which was previously named PLUNC. This gene is the human homolog of the murine (mouse) plunc gene and, similar to its mouse counterpart, is specifically expressed in the airways and nasopharyngeal regions. PLUNC has been shown to inhibit the epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) and also exhibits antimicrobial properties. These functions suggest that PLUNC plays a critical role in the innate immune defense mechanisms of the airways. The ability of PLUNC to regulate ENaC is pH-sensitive, and this regulatory function is impaired in the acidic environment of cystic fibrosis airways. Consequently, defective PLUNC1 function is thought to contribute to the development of lung pathology in patients with cystic fibrosis. Additionally, PLUNC may serve as a potential molecular marker for the detection of micrometastasis in non-small-cell lung cancer.
